subject: Acme RAG eval — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Acme RAG eval — follow-up & next steps

Sarah — thanks again for the time this afternoon. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we can move the eval forward.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: improve internal knowledge-base answers across product docs & support articles while minimizing hallucination.
- Traffic: ~500k queries/month, peak QPS ~15.
- Latency target: 200–400ms p95 for the user-facing generation path.
- Security: data stays in your VPC; S3 connectors ok.

High-level recommendation (for the evaluation)
1) Retriever: FAISS (on-prem / managed) using redwood-embed-1 (512-d). Use an ANN index (HNSW) for production; for the eval we can start with a flat index to establish ground truth.
2) Reranker: two-stage approach — bi-encoder to shortlist (top 200), then cross-encoder reranker for final top 10. If cost is a concern, we can limit cross-encoder to top 50. Recommended models: redwood-cross-1 for highest precision; distil-cross for low-cost experiments.
3) Generator (model fit): redwood-6x for final eval (best quality); redwood-2b-quant as cost-constrained baseline.
4) Prompt sets & benchmarks: please use the attached prompt_sets_v2.zip (contains 5 canonical prompt templates + 5k evaluation queries) and the attached acme-benchmark-results.csv (starter seed results from our demo run).

Metrics / acceptance criteria
- Grounding metric: exact-source attribution rate and topical precision (>90% on initial 1k sample).
- Retrieval metrics: recall@5 >= 92% (target), MRR and R-precision reported.
- Hallucination/factuality: hallucination rate < 2% on the evaluation sample.

Immediate next steps
- I will run the 1k seed eval with the configs above and share a results sheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Can we confirm access to the S3 bucket (read-only) and a point contact for infra? (example: acme-platform@acme.com)
- If useful, let's set a 30-minute sync next week to review results and pick a production config.

Attachments: [Attachment: prompt_sets_v2.zip (zip, 2.1MB)], [Attachment: acme-benchmark-results.csv (CSV, 340KB)]

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks, this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications before you run the 1k seed: 

1) Latency: you note p95 200–400ms for generation — is that including the cross-encoder reranker step, or is that generator-only? Our bar for product is closer to 300ms end-to-end.
2) Cost: can you give a rough cost delta for the cross-encoder rerank vs a single-stage bi-encoder? We want to understand whether we can afford full cross-encoder at scale or should only use it for the top-N fallback.
3) S3 access: I can open a read-only bucket for the eval. I'll loop in our infra team (acme-platform@acme.com) separately.

Also can you share the results sheet link you mentioned? If we can have the 1k seed by tomorrow that'd be great.

Thanks Sarah — quick answers inline: 

> Latency: you note p95 200–400ms for generation — is that including the cross-encoder reranker step, or is that generator-only?

The 200–400ms target is generator-facing (post-rerank). Our recommended production pattern is to do initial retrieval + lightweight bi-encoder shortlist (very low cost) and then a cross-encoder rerank that only processes the top 50 candidates. With that setup we've seen end-to-end p95s ~300–380ms on a dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool (depending on model size); if you need tighter p95 we can use a smaller cross-encoder or move reranker to async/late-arrival for UI fallback.

> Cost: can you give a rough cost delta for the cross-encoder rerank vs a single-stage bi-encoder?

Rough ballpark: full cross-encoder across 200 candidates is ~3–5x the compute cost of a bi-encoder shortlist. Limiting cross-encoder to top 50 brings that to ~1.2–2x depending on model choice. We'll include a cost estimate in the results sheet.

I started the 1k seed run with the configs in my first note — I'll share the Google sheet with the run results in the link below once complete. Proposed time for a quick review call: Thu 2027-04-29 10:00am PT?

Results sheet (will be populated): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_acme-rag-benchmarks
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-3421

If acme-platform confirms S3 access, we'll ingest a small shard and run the FAISS flat index to start.

Attachments referenced above.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Internal note / engineering recs (internal only):

Marissa — good plan. A few concrete suggestions for the seed eval and how we should present the tradeoffs to ACME: 

1) Reranker choice: run both a redwood-cross-1 cross-encoder (high precision) AND a distil-cross (cost baseline). Compare precision@1 and exact-source attribution. For quick cost modeling, assume cross-encoder latency per doc ~12ms (redwood-cross-1) and distil ~4ms.

2) Retrieval settings: start with FAISS flat for the 1k seed to give us deterministic recall numbers (no ANN noise). For production, recommend HNSW with quantization (IVF-PQ) tuned to meet recall@5 >= 92%. Use batch size 256 for embedding generation to keep GPU utilization efficient.

3) Grounding metrics: report exact-source attribution rate, hallucination rate (manually labeled sample), and an automatic entailment-based factuality score. Add per-query trace: top-K sources + reranker score delta so we can identify regressions.

4) Eval plan & timelines: run 1k seed today (Marissa), then expand to 5k within 3 business days if seed looks good. For ACME budget sensitivity, show a two-column table: (a) cost-optimized (distil-cross + top50 rerank) and (b) precision-first (redwood-cross-1 + top200 shortlist).

5) Quick action: if Lukas can stand up FAISS ingest on the small S3 shard today we can have seed results in ~18 hours. I'll prepare a short notebook to compute MRR / recall / R-precision and a script to export the per-query traces.

I'll attach a short sample script to run locally and the query list mapping in the shared drive.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
